attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors measures how much one vector extends in the direction of the other. Geometrically, it equals the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them. If the dot product is zero, the vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular), meaning they have no projection onto each other. A negative dot product indicates that the angle between the vectors is greater than 90 degrees, so one vector projects negatively onto the other, pointing in the opposite direction.

A negative dot product means the angle between the vectors is greater than 90 degrees, so the projection of one vector onto the other points in the opposite direction, indicating a negative projection.
